newsitem.title: USA: New lawsuit could delay Tampa, Fla., stadium bonds.
newsitem.headline: New lawsuit could delay Tampa, Fla., stadium bonds.

text.p: A Hillsborough County, Fla., stadium bond issue could be delayed because a second lawsuit has been filed challenging the use of tax money for the project, County Attorney Emeline Acton said Friday.
The $168 million revenue bond issue by the Tampa Sports Authority was to be priced in late October or early November via Smith Barney Inc.
Acton said the firm would meet Monday with city and county officials and lawyers to decide whether to proceed with the issue.
"Some of my financial advisers are saying you can't even issue bonds with a lawsuit like that pending. Others are saying it wouldn't make any difference," Acton said.

The lawsuit was filed Thursday in Hillsborough Circuit Court by former former Tampa Mayor William Poe, who sued unsuccessfully in August to block a referendum on the sales tax increase that will back the bonds.
The half-cent tax increase was approved by voters on September 3 and would raise $2.7 billion over 30 years for schools, raods, public safety and the stadium.
In the first lawsuit, Circuit Judge James Whittmore upheld the constitutionality of the ballot question.
Poe told the St. Petersburg Times that in the first lawsuit, the judge was legally unable to divide the ballot question into the different elements to be financed with the sales tax.
The new suit asks the judge to focus only on the constitutionality of using public money for the stadium, which Poe said would mainly benefit the private, for-profit football team.
Poe also said the majority of voters who approved the tax had no in-depth understanding of the complex stadium lease hammered out six days before the referendum.
Acton said the lawsuit raises no new issues, and that the county would file a motion to dismiss it later Friday, on grounds that the matter had already been litigated.
"You typically aren't allowed two bites at the same apple in trial court," Acton said.
The deadline to appeal the initial ruling passed at 5 p.m. Thursday, Acton said.
The case was assigned to Circuit Judge Sam Pendino and the county has requested a hearing at 2 p.m. Oct 4, although the hearing date was not final.
Acton said the county had planned to include a summary of the first lawsuit in the official statement, which was still being drafted.
